sources.origin: All values are those of the #15299 prototype's accepted look (2026-11-20 review) on the 1.82 m tour-average subject; lengths in metres.
sources.shirt: A polo 10 mm off the skin and never closer than 6 mm; eight Taubin passes take the muscle relief off the cloth without shrinking it.
sources.trousers: 10 mm off the skin, never closer than 5 mm, relaxed over 30 passes so the cloth bridges the crotch and the knee.
sources.skin_margin_m: The bare skin continues 4 mm under each hem so bending opens no gap.
sources.hem_seam: A hem's rim is the garment's cut line, laid on the skin; the bare skin was cut 4 mm further under the cloth (skin_margin_m), so the rim's points lay inside the skin's faces, not on its vertices. Blend skinning is not linear along an edge whose ends carry different weights, so a posed rim left the posed faces: on a fitted driver swing (showpiece profile, MuJoCo skin, 2026-11-20) the collar rim stood 0.27 to 0.29 mm off the skin between the top and impact with the girdle weights relaxed (pose_settings.json, girdle_smoothing_iterations 45) against 0.15 to 0.16 mm without (0.31 mm at address either way), and a camera level with the hem looked under it into the shirt: 32 see-through pixels in 220 neck close-ups (every 12th frame, four directions, 480 px at 0.6 m) against 7 without the relaxed weights, all but 2 of them on a hem's rim, most on the collar's. A wider margin made it worse (12 mm: 70 pixels), a rim sunk 0.5 mm under the skin hid it (2 pixels). With hem_seam the bare skin is split on the shirt's hem lines before it is cut (the trouser hem is the skin's own end already), so each rim vertex and rim edge of the collar and the sleeve hems is a vertex and an edge of the skin with the same weights, and the two cannot part at any pose: 0.00 mm, 2 pixels (both at a hand, none at the neck). The skin's surface and its end under the cloth are unchanged; it gains the rims' vertices (1500 to 1734 vertices on the default subject). false: the skin as before. limits.hem_seam_mm bounds the largest distance from a rim vertex of the collar and the sleeve hems to the nearest skin vertex with the trail girdle protracted 110 mm and the head turned 0.6 rad (measured 0 with the seam, 7.8 mm without, where the skin has no vertex on the line).
sources.waist_height_m: Waistband top 110 mm above the hip midpoint along the trunk axis; the shirt is tucked tuck_m (50 mm) below it: at 60 mm the tail reached the crease of the hip, where the thigh's cloth turns into it when the hip bends, and showed through the trousers at address and impact (2026-11-20).
sources.sleeve_fraction: A short sleeve ends half way down the upper arm.
sources.trouser_end_fraction: The trouser leg ends 1.05 shank lengths below the knee, 22 mm below the ankle joint on the 1.82 m subject: a trouser that breaks on the shoe (see ankle_end).
sources.ankle_end: The stored skin ends about the ankle in a ragged rim, from 93 % of the shank in front to 101 % at the heel, so a leg cut at 97 % ended 13 to 30 mm above the ankle joint on a ragged line and left a strip of bare ankle over the shoe (showpiece round 10: 103,226 skin pixels in 596 of 880 ankle close-ups over the swing, every 12th frame, each ankle from 8 directions; none after). The rim's vertices are therefore moved along the shank to ankle_end_fraction (1.06) of it before the body is dressed, the trouser leg is cut on that drawn-down leg at trouser_end_fraction, and the bare skin ends on the same line instead of running on under the hem. Limits, measured 2026-11-20 on both fit profiles: bare_ankle_mm, how far bare skin within ankle_reach_m of the shank axis reaches below the hem, 0 (36 mm before in the fitted rest pose; in the MuJoCo model at the address, top, impact and finish poses of tests/fixtures/model_appearance/swing_poses.json, which do not bend the ankle, 16.3 mm before); hem_level_mm, how far the hem's cloth edge lies from that level, 1.4 to 1.6 mm; shoe_overlap_mm, how far the hem ends below the top of the shoe's upper in the MuJoCo model, 19.9 to 24.1 mm (the cut is measured with the left shank's length, and the 1.71 m test subject's right shank is drawn 4 mm longer).
sources.collar: The collar line runs collar_gap_m (12 mm) from the line where the stored skin crosses the neck joint's height (the exact crossing on each face, not the mesh edges about it, whose zigzag of one edge length the hem used to repeat) and collar_front_drop_m (30 mm) lower in front, reached collar_front_reach_m (60 mm) ahead of that line's centre along a smoothstep, so the hem has no corner where the drop starts or ends.
sources.neck_hug: At the collar the shirt is held to neck_hug_m (5 mm) off the skin; the allowed ease grows by neck_hug_gain per metre below the collar line.
sources.sleeve_hug: At the sleeve end the shirt is held to sleeve_hug_m (5 mm, the same as at the collar) off the arm, and the allowed ease grows by sleeve_hug_gain (0.2) per metre up the sleeve, back to the full ease 25 mm above the hem: the hem sits on the arm, and its folded edge is 5 mm wide instead of a 10 mm ring standing off it (2026-11-20 close-up review).
sources.tuck: From tuck_band_m[0] (30 mm) above the waistband the shirt ease is capped at tuck_ease_m[0] (12 mm), falling over tuck_band_m[1] (50 mm) to tuck_ease_m[1] (4 mm) under the trousers.
sources.wrist_cut_m: The stored skin ends where MakeHuman's hand weights take over, a ragged rim from 8.2 mm before to 10.2 mm past the wrist joint (measured on the default subject, 2026-11-20). Cutting on a plane 10 mm before the joint clears all of it; the hand model's forearm cuff reaches about 60 mm up the forearm and covers the ring.
sources.chest: The chest front of the trunk: from chest.from_m (130 mm, 20 mm above the waistband top so the hem keeps its line) above the hip midpoint to above_shoulders_m (40 mm) above the shoulder joints, half_width_m (170 mm) either side of the midline, from ahead_m (30 mm) ahead of the trunk axis, each edge ramped over edge_m (30 mm). There the body is moved fore and aft to its area-weighted mean depth within smooth_sigma_m (35 mm, about half a pectoral) and the shirt is relaxed for tent_passes (60) passes, never under its floor ease: the creases between and under the pectorals fill, as taut cloth does. The #15299 prototype's values (2026-11-20 review).
sources.sleeve_cap: Within sleeve_cap_m (110 mm, the deltoid) of a shoulder joint the shirt is relaxed the same way for sleeve_cap_passes (20) passes, which takes the crease between deltoid and chest off the sleeve cap.
sources.leg_tube: Each trouser leg is held at least leg_tube_m[0] (68 mm) off the shank axis at the knee and leg_tube_m[1] (56 mm) at the ankle, falling to nothing leg_tube_rise (0.5) shank lengths above the knee: a straight leg instead of cloth that follows calf and ankle (bare shank radius 30 to 60 mm on the 1.82 m subject). The #15299 prototype's 78 and 66 mm gave a hem of at least 41 cm and read baggy under the slim trunk (round-9 review); 68 and 56 mm give one of 35 cm, a tapered golf trouser, and the cloth still keeps its floor ease off the calf.
sources.limits: Test bounds, measured 2026-11-20 on the 1.82 m reference subject (tests/unit/model_appearance/test_body_skin_dress.py). Pectoral relief: how far the shirt over a pectoral (pectoral_span_m off the midline) stands ahead of the shirt on the sternum, the largest over relief_heights_m above the hip midpoint: 0.6 mm (default fit) and 0.8 mm (showpiece) against 11.1 and 9.9 mm without the chest steps. Crease: largest depth of a shirt vertex under the mean of its neighbours, on the chest and within cap_radius_m of a shoulder joint: 0.03 mm against 1.3 and 1.0 mm. Chest depth: fore-aft extent of the shirt within 50 mm of the midline at chest_depth_heights_m, measured 257 and 246 mm (default fit) and 228 and 200 mm (showpiece, with its slim build; 243 and 225 mm before the slim build was mixed in), 7 to 9 mm less than without the chest steps. Hem roughness: largest distance of a hem loop's points from its fit with hem_harmonics (6) harmonics of arc length; the collar measured 2.0 and 2.1 mm (default fit, rim and cloth edge) and 1.8 and 1.9 mm (showpiece), against 4.6 and 4.9 mm and 4.4 and 4.8 mm when the collar was measured from the mesh edges. Sleeve hem stand: distance of the cloth edge from its rim on the arm, 5.0 to 5.1 mm against 10.0 mm before the sleeve hug.
sources.neck_cap: The skin's neck ends in an open ring along the jawline (50 edges on the default subject, 5 to 12 mm above the neck joint in front, 90 mm behind) that takes only part of a head turn, while the head model is rigid: behind the jaw a camera saw between the two and through the head. The ring is drawn tuck_m (20 mm) towards a point apex_forward_m (20 mm) ahead of and apex_height_m (110 mm) above the neck joint, the skin within tuck_span_m (30 mm) of it less, so the neck goes in under the jaw instead of standing off it as a ledge. A plug closes it: the ring again, evened out along its loop (lip_passes, 10) and lip_m (12 mm) nearer the point, and the point. The whole plug carries the ring's mean weights: it follows the neck's end as one piece, an affine image of its rest shape, and cannot fold in itself. Tried first and dropped (2026-11-20, default subject, head turned 1.4 rad): a point rigid with the head folds the closing faces and turns the ring's normals, so the head base check of export_settings.json read 10.6 mm outside; a ring whole on the head, 31 mm; a second ring with the first ring's own weights, 13 to 18 mm. With the plug that check read what it did without (3.7 and 4.7 mm inside) for a head base held in a 30 mm circle; the elliptic base that followed reaches further forward than the drawn-in neck allows and was shortened in front for it (export_settings.json, head_base: 1.0 and 1.7 mm inside). lip_m 6 mm folds up to 19 faces of the skin at a swing pose, 12 mm at most 10 (5 without the plug; swing_limits.folded_share allows 19). tuck_m was 14 mm; there the skin near its end ran 2 to 5 mm inside the head model's wall behind the jaw corner and the ear and the two cut each other in saw teeth, at 20 mm it goes in under the head at a clear angle (close-ups of a fitted driver swing, 2026-11-20); at 24 mm a plug vertex came 0.04 mm outside the neck with the head turned 1.4 rad (limits.neck_plug.outside_m). apex_height_m 0 leaves the neck open.
sources.neck_plug: Checks of neck_cap in the MuJoCo model (tests/unit/motion_matching/test_mujoco_body_skin.py) at the address, top and finish poses with the head turned turns_rad. Open end: length of open skin edge within reach_m of the head body that lies more than bare_m from the shirt, so that no collar covers it; measured 2026-11-20 on the default subject 471 to 509 mm without the plug (at least open_end_m) and none with it, the rest of the open edge (the rim under the collar) at most 11.7 mm from the shirt. outside_m: no plug vertex may lie outside the neck (signed distance along the nearest skin vertex's normal, plug faces left out); measured 0.6 to 5.7 mm inside. collar_m: least distance from the plug to the shirt, measured 38.6 to 69.9 mm. The plug's point must be covered by the head model (each of rays directions over the head's upper half meets the shell) and lie apex_depth_m under it; measured 36.8 to 44.2 mm.
sources.waist_gap: From waistband_span_m[0] (70 mm) below the waistband top each trouser vertex is put on the normal through the shirt's cloth over the same body point, at least waist_gap_m (6 mm) outside it (below the shirt's tail: that far outside the tail's ease). The two garments used to be draped apart: the trousers' relaxation slid their vertices along the body, so the same skin weights no longer moved the same points, and the shirt came through the trousers when the trunk turned and the hips bent. Measured 2026-11-20 on the showpiece profile at the address, top, impact and finish poses of tests/fixtures/model_appearance/swing_poses.json: 7 to 11 of 362 shirt samples below the waistband line outside the trousers, by up to 3.3 mm, before; none after. Limits: tucked_margin_mm is the least height of a trouser vertex of that band over the shirt in the fitted rest pose (measured 5.1 mm on both fit profiles, against 0.3 and 1.3 mm before), tucked_margin_posed_mm the same at those four poses (measured 2.4 to 3.7 mm, against -1.6 to 0.4 mm before). shank_slack_mm bounds the mean radius of the trouser cloth about the shank axis less the bare leg's, between 0.3 and 0.7 of the shank and between 0.7 and trouser_end_fraction (measured 17.1 and 20.0 mm with the leg ending at 1.05; 16.8 and 21.3 mm when it ended at 0.97, against 22.8 and 30.8 mm with the 78 and 66 mm tube).
sources.waistband: The trousers' floor ease grows by waistband_m (6 mm) from waistband_span_m[0] (70 mm) below the waistband top over waistband_span_m[1] (40 mm), so the band always covers the tucked shirt.
